name: Four Seasons Hotel New York
insider_take: Towering 52 stories above Manhattan's buzzing energy, this limestone fortress houses one of the city's most coveted addresses—where A-listers slip in through private entrances and power brokers seal deals over champagne.
whats_special: The hotel occupies floors 30-52 of the iconic I.M. Pei-designed tower, offering unparalleled Central Park and city skyline views. Its Ty Warner Penthouse, once the world's most expensive hotel suite at $60,000 per night, features 360-degree Manhattan views and a private spa treatment room.
pro_tip: Book a park-facing room on floors 35+ for stunning sunrise views over the reservoir, and time your arrival for the golden hour when Central Park transforms into a glowing emerald carpet below.
dont_miss: The Garden restaurant's three-course Central Park view dining experience, and a visit to the 52nd-floor spa—the highest hotel spa in NYC—where floor-to-ceiling windows create a floating-in-the-clouds sensation during treatments.
pros: Prime Midtown Manhattan location near Central Park and Fifth Avenue shopping
Legendary Four Seasons white-glove service and attention to detail
Spacious luxury rooms and suites with marble bathrooms
Award-winning Ty Bar and fine dining restaurant on-site
cons: Premium luxury pricing reflects Manhattan location
Busy Midtown area can be crowded with tourists
